findings.claim: Section 5 transitions REVIEWING directly to ACCEPTED with no acceptance-authority guard, while Sections 4/12.6/12.7 and P16 make acceptance an attributable HUMAN act, and Section 10's ownership policy declares no write mechanism for the acceptance transition; the acceptance control surface therefore has no modelled owner/guard, fail state or recovery path.
findings.impact: A literal implementation of the lifecycle can record ACCEPTED as a consequence of the REVIEWING outcome, so acceptance state can change without the attributable HUMAN acceptance owner required by P16; the transition also lacks the owner, exact evidence, fail state and recovery path that must_check 4 requires for every control surface, and the reject branch in Section 14 has no modelled lifecycle state.
findings.recommended_action: Add an explicit acceptance transition in Section 5 guarded by the exact HUMAN acceptance owner or a non-revoked HUMAN delegation decision, with its accept/reject fail states and recovery, and add the acceptance record's owning command or permitted file operation plus evidence and verifier to the Section 10 ownership policy and the P16 receipt.

rejected_candidates.reason: P14 charge-guard completeness: Section 5.2 steps 1-2 do not enumerate P13/P15/P16 revocation/scope re-verification. Rejected because step 1 re-hashes every bundle input under the bundle's sealed freshness_rule and predicate scope and P14 is a binding pre-charge invariant with EXPIRED disposition, so no path to charge with a revoked authority is established.

Budget contingency floor: Section 7.1 says the next WBS 'must reserve at least' two attempts but 'only the HUMAN decision owner may select or change the operative amount', so P12 could pass on a HUMAN-chosen lower reserve. Rejected because must_check 11 reserves ceiling/reallocation to the HUMAN as an explicit recorded decision and the operative reserve stays exposed rather than hidden.

Bundle identity hash: Section 6.2 invalidation records carry bundle_sha256 while Section 6 says READY, invalidation records and the charge boundary identify the bundle by the seal-sidecar full-file SHA-256 and bind the sidecar hash as well. Rejected because the text requires both the bundle full-file hash and the sidecar hash to be bound, so an invalidation cannot be skipped by hash selection.

Sequencing: Section 7.1 orders drafting after design closure and before budget/approval binding, while Section 16 places migration and bootstrap completion before drafting. Rejected because drafting is uncharged, inactive and grants no selection, admission or attempt authority, so the ordering difference cannot permit charge or acceptance.

Section 5.2 step 3 permits recording unavailable evidence 'outside mission controls' without a declared path or owner. Rejected because it writes no mission-control, ledger, product or acceptance bytes and therefore cannot permit charge or acceptance.
